items.title: Denmark sends conscripts to Greenland as Arctic tensions grow
items.summary: KANGERLUSSUAQ: For the first time in recent history, Danish conscripts have been deployed to Greenland, as Denmark moves to bolster its presence in the Arctic after US demands to acquire the territory. US President Donald Trump has repeatedly sought to acquire the semi-autonomous Danish island, citing national security concerns and accusing Copenhagen of neglecting Arctic defence. Denmark and Greenland have firmly rejected the idea.

items.title: Steel Hawk earnings visibility cloudy despite RM576mil tender book
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Steel Hawk Bhd's orderbook visibility remains limited in the near term despite its sizeable tender pipeline, as the company remains cautious about the oil and gas (O&G) environment. TA Securities said Steel Hawk's current orderbook of RM63.4 million provides some revenue visibility going into the second half of the year (2H FY26), but remains relatively modest compared with its RM575.8 million tender book. "While this broadens Steel Hawk's addressable market, a meaningful portion of the potential growth remains dependent on securing new awards, with management guiding to only 10–20 per cent conversion of the tender book.

items.title: MACC: Six Felda and FIC cases under investigation, arrests imminent
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 2 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has opened six new investigation papers into alleged misappropriation, abuse of power and corruption involving the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) and its subsidiary, Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC), with several arrests expected beginning next week. MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the investigations followed information received on Aug 24 regarding the implementation of projects and investments by Felda and FIC management between 2010 and 2020. The six matters are the purchase of Tataran Aras Sdn Bhd in Limbang, Sarawak; the acquisition of Grand Borneo Hotel Sdn Bhd in Sabah; the purchase of Grand Plaza Serviced Apartments in London; the establishment of Felda Wellness Corporation Sdn Bhd; the acquisition of Felda House and Grand Felda House; and alleged misappropriation in the development of the Kuala Lumpur Vertical City (KLVC) project.

items.title: Nepal tunnel rescuers seek trapped workers but hit dead ends
items.summary: KATHMANDU: Nepali rescuers searched Wednesday for survivors feared trapped inside hydropower tunnels a week after devastating floods, but hopes were fading as teams hit dead ends and no one was confirmed alive. The government had said intially it believed that more than 100 workers could be alive inside multiple tunnels. "The search and rescue operation is still underway, and foreign teams are also supporting it at the hydropower tunnels," said Shanti Mahat, spokeswoman of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA).

items.title: Bangladeshi minister's 200,000-worker claim not official govt position – Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: A Bangladeshi minister's claim that Malaysia plans to recruit 200,000 Bangladeshi workers over the next six months does not represent the official position of the Bangladeshi government, says government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. Yesterday, Bangladeshi Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Junior Minister Mir Shahe Alam said Malaysia planned to recruit about 200,000 Bangladeshi workers over the next six months. In June, Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman urged Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to consider reopening Malaysia's labour market to Bangladeshi workers.

items.title: 'Saint Seiya' anime author claims former aide embezzled US$29m
items.summary: TOKYO: The Japanese author of globally popular manga series "Saint Seiya", Masami Kurumada, said Wednesday he was suing a former business associate for allegedly embezzling US$29 million. Kurumada, 72, said the former manager responsible for the accounting of the artist's businesses siphoned off the sum over more than 10 years. The former manager has returned 1.8 billion yen (US$11.3 million) of the 4.68 billion yen he is alleged to have embezzled, according to local media.

items.title: Fomca advises public to limit outdoor activities amid haze
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A consumer watchdog has advised Malaysians to limit outdoor activities and strenuous exercise when air quality reaches unhealthy levels amid continuing haze. "Haze is not merely about poor visibility. It is about the quality of the air that millions of people breathe every day," the Federation of Malaysian Consumers Associations (Fomca) chief executive officer Dr T. Saravanan told the New Straits Times.

items.title: Jakim backs decision over 'Madu atau Racun', lodges report with MCMC
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Islamic Development Department (Jakim) has backed the decision by the Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) to reject the airing of Madu atau Racun , a drama series. Jakim said the decision was justified as the drama, which is available on the iQIYI platform, featured elements that contradicted religious and cultural values, sparking public concern. Jakim has lodged a report with the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC).

items.title: [UPDATED] Former TH COO Adi Azuan expected to be charged tomorrow
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Former Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) chief operating officer Datuk Adi Azuan Abdul Ghani is expected to be charged at the Sessions Court here tomorrow. Adi Azuan joined TH in July 2002 as its group accounts divisional head before later becoming its chief operating officer. The four others were former group chief financial officer Datuk Rozaida Omar, former senior general manager of corporate services and property Rifina Md Ariff, former chief human resources officer Mohd Hisham Harun and former legal adviser Hazlina Mohd Khalid.

items.title: Iran's top negotiator calls US 'Satan' after wedding attack
items.summary: TEHERAN: Iran's top negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf on Wednesday called the United States "Satan" after an attack on a wedding ceremony in the country's south. "If a power acts like Satan, picks targets like Satan, and kills like Satan, it's Satan. It's THE Great Satan," said Ghalibaf in a post on X, referring to the US and key ally Israel.

items.title: More than 2,000 PBM members quit to join Wawasan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: More than 2,000 Parti Bangsa Malaysia (PBM) members announced their decision to join Parti Wawasan Negara today. Former PBM national youth chief Hanis Asmui said the move followed the dissolution of the party's central, state, and division youth committees effective immediately today. He said the decision was made unanimously, voluntarily, and without coercion or pressure from any party.

items.title: Perak police launch investigations over toddler’s fatal fall at Victoria Bridge
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 2 — Police have opened two investigation papers into the death of a three-year-old boy who is believed to have fallen about five metres from Victoria Bridge in Enggor, near Kuala Kangsar, yesterday. Perak Police Chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the investigation papers were opened under Section 31(1) of the Child Act 2001, with several individuals summoned to assist the investigation. Meanwhile, State Housing and Local Government Committee chairperson Sandrea Ng Shy Ching said the Kuala Kangsar Municipal Council (MPKK) had immediately closed visitor access to the steel structure section of the bridge as a safety measure.

items.title: High Court dismisses Malaysian Bar bid to challenge HRD Corp levy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court has dismissed the Malaysian Bar's judicial review challenging the application of the Human Resources Development Corporation (HRD Corp) levy and training framework to the legal profession. Judge Alice Loke ruled that there was no conflict between the Pembangunan Sumber Manusia Berhad Act 2001 (PSMB Act) and the Legal Profession Act 1976 (LPA). She said the PSMB Act complemented the Malaysian Bar's role in providing training to members of the legal profession by allocating a specific fund for that purpose.

items.title: MACC investigator: Muhyiddin abused powers as PM to help Jana Wibawa contractors
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — Former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin abused his powers as a prime minister when he acted to help Bumiputera contractors to eventually get government projects under the Jana Wibawa programme, an anti-corruption investigator told the High Court. When asked by Wan Shaharuddin to explain why he said Muhyiddin had abused his powers as prime minister, Mazery said this was due to Muhyiddin’s actions in relation to companies who were applying for Jana Wibawa projects. Muhyiddin was prime minister from March 1, 2020 until Aug 20, 2021.

items.title: Don’t sacrifice independent oversight for speed in Sabah’s water crisis fixes, says former Water Dept director
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 2 — Sabah’s recurring water supply problems require urgent and practical solutions, but the push for faster action should not come at the expense of independent engineering judgement, said Datuk Amarjit Singh. The former Sabah Water Department director said a clear distinction must be maintained between an engineering consultancy practice and a commercial service provider, particularly when companies supplying water infrastructure, equipment, or specialised technologies are also proposing solutions. Amarjit said companies recommending technologies in which they have a commercial interest could face an inherent potential conflict, making independent assessment important.

items.title: Khazanah delegation visits Media Prima headquarters
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Khazanah Nasional Berhad managing director Datuk Amirul Feisal Wan Zahir today led a delegation on a corporate visit to Balai Berita, the headquarters of Media Prima Berhad, to strengthen engagement and gain an insight into the group's media, news, digital and content operations. The delegation was welcomed by Media Prima group managing director Datuk Rafiq Razali, Media Prima Content and TV Networks and Primeworks Studios chief executive officer Nini Yusof, Media Prima News and Current Affairs group managing editor Jasbant Singh, and Media Prima News and Current Affairs deputy group managing editor and New Straits Times group editor Datuk Farrah Naz Karim. The delegation toured Media Prima Audio, the News & Current Affairs studios, WHI studio, Rev Media Group and the editorial floor housing KLIK, where they were briefed on the group's operations across broadcasting, news, digital media and content production.

items.title: High Court rejects citizenship bid by woman born out of wedlock to Malaysian father
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Muar High Court has dismissed a woman's bid for Malaysian citizenship by operation of law despite her biological father being a Malaysian citizen. Kalyana said the court was bound by the Federal Court's ruling, which had authoritatively settled the constitutional interpretation governing citizenship for children born out of wedlock. "The applicant's biological father is undoubtedly a Malaysian citizen.

items.title: 1,476 Myanmar refugees signed documents for voluntary repatriation
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The 1,476 Myanmar refugees set to be repatriated at the end of this month have signed documents stating that they voluntarily wish to return, said government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. Fahmi said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan had briefed the cabinet on the matter, explaining that the figure was determined through a screening process involving more than 10,000 Myanmar refugees held at immigration detention depots. "5,000 names were (then) screened by the Home Ministry, and these 5,000 names were then forwarded to the Myanmar embassy.

items.title: Federal Court grants govt, police leave to appeal death-in-custody rulings
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Federal Court here today granted the government and police leave to appeal against a ruling that held them liable for the death of gravedigger Mohd Fadzrin Zaidi, who was found hanging in a police lock-up in 2019. In Fadzrin's case, the government and police sought leave to appeal against the Court of Appeal's decision of Jan 26 this year, which had affirmed the High Court's ruling holding them liable for his death. The court also held the government vicariously liable for that negligence and awarded Fadhelah RM147,600 in damages.

items.title: Batik Air agrees to resume Miri-KL flights after deputy minister’s request
items.summary: MIRI, Sept 2 — Batik Air has agreed to resume its Miri-Kuala Lumpur services following a formal request by Deputy Minister of Tourism, Arts and Culture Chiew Choon Man. The Miri MP said the commencement date, flight frequency and schedule would be announced by the airline in due course. Chiew said he had received increasing feedback from Miri residents over the difficulty of securing flights between Miri and Kuala Lumpur, particularly during weekends, public holidays and peak travel periods.

items.title: Retiree loses RM1.417m after transferring savings across multiple accounts in phone‑call scam
items.summary: Pahang acting police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the victim, a 66-year-old man, received a call from an unknown individual on May 19 who claimed that the victim was involved in money laundering activities. He said the victim was then instructed to open an Agrobank account and transfer his savings to the account for the purpose of checking by the authorities. “After opening the account, a man came to meet the victim in his residential area and the victim handed over his bank card and PIN number to the man,” he said in a statement.

items.title: US embassy shifts Sabah travel status to ‘relaxed’ after security improvements
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 2 — The United States is encouraging its citizens and international travellers to visit Sabah, citing significant improvements in security and a corresponding relaxation of travel advisories, said US Embassy Kuala Lumpur Chargé d'Affaires David Gamble. Many countries are following America’s lead and reviewing their travel advisories as well,” Gamble said during the launch of the Freedom 250 Sabah programme at the Tanjung Aru State Library today. We want to encourage more tourists to visit Sabah because Sabah is a wonderful place to visit.”

items.title: [UPDATED]: CMCF to meet 'Madu atau Racun' producers, iQIYI over controversial content
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Communications and Multimedia Content Forum Malaysia (CMCF) will meet the producers of controversial drama series 'Madu atau Racun' and streaming platform iQIYI to obtain a comprehensive explanation regarding its content. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the government has made the directive and it would not compromise with any production party that touched on religious and racial sensitivities. However, he said, over-the-top (OTT) streaming platforms via the internet were not yet fully subject to the same licensing framework.

items.title: 77 Malaysians found safe in Tibet, Nepal being repatriated
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The 77 Malaysians found safe in Tibet and Nepal following last week's flash floods are being brought to Kathmandu for repatriation to Malaysia, said government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, adding that 55 Malaysians have yet to be traced. "Meanwhile, 77 Malaysians have been located in Tibet and Nepal. Fahmi said the cabinet took note of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's approval of a US$1 million contribution towards humanitarian efforts.

items.title: Johor dengue cases jump 131pc to 9,954 as infections rise across districts
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 2 — Johor recorded 9,954 dengue cases as of Epid Week (ME) 34 this year, an increase of 131.3 per cent compared to 4,304 cases for the same period last year. State Health and Environment Committee Chairman Ling Tian Soon said of the total, 4,520 cases or 45.4 per cent were reported from outbreak localities while 5,434 cases or 54.6 per cent were from non-outbreak localities. “Of the total dengue cases reported throughout ME34, 308 cases or 46.4 per cent were reported from outbreak localities and 356 cases or 53.6 per cent from non-outbreak localities,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Boat operator arrested, remanded four days over Mersing collision
items.summary: MERSING: A 33-year-old boat operator was remanded for four days from today to assist investigations into a collision involving two passenger boats at Kuala Sungai Mersing on Monday. Police obtained the four-day remand order from the Kota Tinggi magistrate's court, with the remand order running from today until Sept 5 under Section 117 of the Criminal Procedure Code. Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the suspect had a previous criminal record involving a drug offence.

items.title: [UPDATED] Malaysia Day celebrations to be held indoors in Kuching amid haze
items.summary: Malaysia Day celebrations on Sept 16 will be held indoors at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK) due to worsening haze conditions in Sarawak, government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. Meanwhile, on cloud seeding operations in Sarawak, Fahmi said the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry had informed the Cabinet that operations were subject to recommendations from the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), based on the detection of clouds suitable for seeding. This, Fahmi added, meant any seeding conducted would not produce rainfall in the areas that needed it most.

items.title: One teen found dead as search continues for three others missing in Tanjung Balau
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 2 — The body of one of four teenagers feared drowned at Tanjung Lompat Beach in Tanjung Balau was recovered this afternoon. The victim, identified as Alif Taqiudin Kamal Hasrul Mohamad, was found by the search and rescue (SAR) team and members of the public at 1.25pm, approximately 800 metres from the location where he was last seen. Kota Tinggi police chief Deputy Superintendent Mohd Syamsuri Mohamad confirmed that the body was identified by family members and has since been transported to Kota Tinggi Hospital.

items.title: Businessman loses safe, Mercedes in RM550,000 break-in
items.summary: SUNGAI PETANI: A businessman suffered losses of about RM550,000 after his house in Taman Seri Jenaris, Tikam Batu, was broken into and a safe and his Mercedes were stolen early yesterday. Kuala Muda police chief Assistant Commissioner Hanyan Ramlan said the victim realised his house had been broken into when he returned home around noon. Hanyan said the house was not equipped with closed-circuit television (CCTV), but police received information from members of the public who claimed to have seen three individuals suspected of being involved in the incident.

items.title: Man held for allegedly assaulting wife after she refused to give him gambling money
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: A 35-year-old man was remanded for three days from today for allegedly assaulting his wife after she refused to give him money to gamble online. The incident occurred at 4am on Aug 31 at a house in Rengit after the suspect allegedly became angry and struck the woman several times on the head, causing injuries. Preliminary investigations found that the suspect allegedly assaulted the woman after she refused to give him money for online gambling.

items.title: MMEA detains tugboat and dredger over suspected ship‑to‑ship transfer; RM260m oil cargo seized off Tanjung Buai
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 2 — The Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) detained two vessels suspected of carrying out unauthorised ship-to-ship activities in national waters early yesterday morning, with the value of the seized goods estimated at RM260 million. Tanjung Sedili Zone Maritime acting director Maritime Commander Mohd Najib Sam said the action was carried out at 3.20am after receiving public information regarding two suspicious vessels seen huddled together at a position about 1.4 nautical miles northwest of Tanjung Buai. Mohd Najib said the tugboat was operated by a crew of five including the skipper, consisting of local and Indonesian citizens aged between 26 and 58 years, while the dredger was operated by a crew of 13 including the skipper, all local citizens aged between 22 and 51 years.

items.title: Missing Nepal climber's family gets support from Penang reps
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Bukit Gelugor member of parliament Ramkarpal Singh and Seri Delima assemblyman Connie Tan visited the family of missing climber Muhammad Muhaimin Azhad Noor Hadi, 27, today. "We understand the difficult situation the family is going through. Ramkarpal contributed RM2,000 to the family, while Tan donated RM1,000.

items.title: VIPs and officials in crosshairs as MACC readies charges for multiple suspects in TH probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) is moving to charge several individuals over the next two days following a massive probe into the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji (TH). MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said that the upcoming charges centre on the alleged abuse of power and misappropriation of RM334.2 million linked to investments in TH Marine, TH Alam, and TH Alam Management, FMT reported. “Another charge involves alleged corruption related to TH’s 30 per cent stake in construction company Putrajaya Perdana Bhd.

items.title: 'We are distraught, worried about Muhaimin's fate in Nepal,' says father
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The family of missing Malaysian climber Muhammad Muhaimin Azhad Noor Hadi, 27, remains distraught over his fate as the search for him continues in Nepal. His father, Noor Hadi Mohd Hassan, 62, said the family was also worried by the lack of updates on the search and rescue (SAR) operation to locate Muhaimin and his two friends. Noor Hadi said Muhaimin was a kind, cheerful and responsible son who played an important role in helping the family with various matters.

items.title: Man remanded after viral video of provocative act at National Day celebration in Putrajaya
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 2 — A man in his 30s, believed to be involved in a provocative incident during the 69th National Day celebrations last Monday, has been remanded for one day starting today. Putrajaya police chief Assistant Commissioner Aidi Sham Mohamed confirmed the arrest when contacted. “The suspect has been remanded for one day starting today,” he said.

items.title: MACC urges Felda to appoint forensic audit team over governance issues
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has urged Felda to appoint its own forensic audit team to investigate governance weaknesses and misconduct within the agency. MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said other enforcement agencies should also examine the weaknesses identified to ensure continuous efforts to prevent misconduct and embezzlement. "For other investigative work, enforcement agencies besides MACC can also assist.

items.title: Hannah Yeoh’s official website confirms divorce after 18-year marriage
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh and her husband Ramachandran Muniandy have divorced after 18 years of marriage. Yeoh was later appointed Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) in December 2025. Within DAP, Yeoh currently serves as deputy secretary-general, vice-chair of DAP and a committee member of DAP Wanita.

items.title: MACC reopens probe into seven Felda cases following new leads
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Seven Felda-related cases previously investigated or highlighted in forensic reports have been reopened after new information emerged, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) said. MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the new leads provided grounds for the commission to re-examine the cases. 3.Merdeka Palace Hotel and Suites – The purchase of the hotel in Kuching, Sarawak, was among Felda Investment Corporation (FIC) property transactions investigated by MACC.

items.title: 18 arrested, 11 remanded in Tabung Haji RCI probes
items.summary: Those arrested included a 61-year-old former managing director of Lembaga Tabung Haji (LTH), a 59-year-old director of Putrajaya Perdana and a 61-year-old former director of Putrajaya Perdana Construction Sdn Bhd. Also arrested were a 60-year-old former chairman of LTH, a 69-year-old former director of Putrajaya Perdana Berhad and a 67-year-old chief operating officer of Alam Maritim Sdn Bhd. The MACC also arrested a 65-year-old former senior general manager of LTH's Haj Division.

items.title: Two arrested after newborn found in sanitary bin at Penang airport
items.summary: BAYAN LEPAS: Police have arrested two people after a newborn baby boy was found alive inside a sanitary bin at Penang International Airport yesterday. Southwest district police chief Assistant Commissioner Anuwal Ab Wahab said the baby was discovered by a cleaner after the worker heard crying from inside the bin at a toilet for persons with disabilities. Anuwal said police investigations, including a review of closed-circuit television (CCTV) recordings, led to the woman's arrest at Kompleks Bukit Jambul.

items.title: ‘Not a coincidence’: Contractors’ RM25.3m to Bersatu came after Muhyiddin’s aid to get projects, was not ‘political donation’, court told
items.summary: Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) investigating officer Mazery Mohd Zaini said the RM25.3 million was instead a reward given after Bersatu president and former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin helped these companies get government projects. Mazery said this while testifying as the 29th prosecution witness in Muhyiddin’s abuse‑of‑power and money‑laundering trial. Mazery said the RM25.3 million was not a genuine donation.

items.title: Strong waves raise beach danger as search continues for four teens
items.summary: The warning comes as four 16-year-old boys remain missing after getting into difficulty while swimming at Tanjung Lompat beach in Tanjung Balau, Penawar, here, this morning. Johor Fire and Rescue Department director Siti Rohani Nadir said rough seas, strong currents and increased recreational activity during the school break could heighten the risk of accidents. "Most drowning incidents occur during school holidays and camping activities at campsites along the coastal areas from Tanjung Balau to Desaru," she said.

items.title: US encourages tourists to visit Sabah as security improves
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The United States is encouraging its citizens and visitors from around the world to travel to Sabah, following improvements in security and a more relaxed travel status for Borneo, said US Embassy Chargé d'Affaires to Malaysia David Gamble. "We want to see more tourists from around the world come here because Sabah is a fantastic place to visit," he told reporters after launching the Freedom 250 campaign in Sabah at the state library in Tanjung Aru near here. In February, the embassy lowered its travel advisory for Eastern Sabah to Level 1 for its citizens, advising them to exercise normal precautions, and Level 2 for the islands and maritime areas off the coast of Eastern Sabah.

items.title: OGX Group taps enterprise AI market with Axtraction tie-up
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: OGX Group Bhd's wholly-owned unit, OGX Networks Sdn Bhd, has entered into a distribution agreement with Axtraction AI Sdn Bhd to market and distribute enterprise artificial intelligence (AI) solutions in Malaysia. "This partnership is expected to strengthen OGX's technology portfolio by expanding into enterprise AI solutions, complementing the company's existing network, cybersecurity and enterprise data centre offerings," it said in a statement. OGX said the partnership will cover Axtraction AI's core platform offerings, including Investigation Decision AI for law enforcement and regulatory agencies, as well as Finance Operation AI for large enterprises.

items.title: Sabah activates state and district disaster command centres as API readings rise to unhealthy levels
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 2 — Sabah has activated its State Disaster Operations Command Centre (PKOB), as well as district-level PKOBs in Kota Kinabalu, Keningau and Papar, as the Air Pollutant Index (API) rose yesterday. State Secretary Datuk Zainudin Aman, who is also State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) chairman, said that API readings reached worrying unhealthy levels yesterday in Kota Kinabalu (177), Tawau (153), Keningau (165), Kimanis, Papar (166) and Kota Kinabalu Polytechnic (153). Zainudin said a haze emergency or disaster would be declared when API readings reached 500 and above.

items.title: PPC orders formation of special task force to probe Penang ferry-cargo vessel collision
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 2 — Authorities have ordered the formation of a special task force to investigate last night’s collision between the Teluk Bahang Ferry and cargo vessel MV Mekar Jaya in Penang Port waters. Penang Port Commission (PPC) Chairman Datuk Yeoh Soon Hin said the task force would investigate the cause of the incident and determine the circumstances surrounding the collision. Yeoh said relevant parties have also been instructed to gather information and assist with compensation matters.

items.title: Tabung Haji RCI: Former minister remanded five days in Saudi Arabia hotel lease probe
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 2 — A former minister has been remanded for five days to assist investigations into a hotel lease issue involving Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) in Saudi Arabia. The remand order, which runs from today until Sunday, was issued against the individual, who is in his 60s, by Magistrate Ezrene Zakariah after the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) made the application at the Magistrate’s Court here today. MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman, when contacted, confirmed the arrest and said the case was being investigated under Section 16(a)(A) of the MACC Act 2009.

items.title: Ambulance driver charged with reckless driving over fatal Jasin crash pleads not guilty
items.summary: JASIN, Sept 2 — An ambulance driver pleaded not guilty at the Magistrate’s Court here today to a charge of reckless driving that resulted in the death of an 18-year-old motorcyclist last week. The prosecution, conducted by Prosecuting Officer Inspector Mohd Hafiz Othman, proposed RM8,000 bail with one surety and a temporary suspension of the accused’s driving licence. Magistrate Mazana Sinin set bail at RM3,000 and allowed the additional condition on his driving licence.

items.title: Prime Minister’s Department blocks airing of ‘Madu atau Racun’ over religious‑sensitivity concerns
items.summary: Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Senator Zulkifli Hasan expressed regret over the inclusion of elements that touched on religious sensitivities and local cultural norms, whether explicitly or implicitly. “The inclusion of elements contrary to Islamic teachings and Eastern cultural values must be curbed to ensure that the faith and moral values of the community, particularly the young generation, remain safeguarded,” he said in a statement today. He said Islamic principles uphold the sanctity of the family institution and the decorum of religious life, while depictions of deviant lifestyles are contrary to these noble values.

items.title: Kelantan’s Nik Mohamad Abduh begins second Senate term after taking oath of office
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — Former Bachok MP Nik Mohamad Abduh Nik Abdul Aziz took his oath of office as a senator for a second term today before Dewan Negara President Datuk Awang Bemee Awang Ali Basah at the Senate chamber in Parliament. Nik Mohamad Abduh was re-elected by the Kelantan State Legislative Assembly under Article 45(1)(a) of the Federal Constitution for a three-year term, effective from July 7, 2026, to July 6, 2029. The son of the late Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Nik Abdul Aziz Nik Mat had previously served as a senator representing Kelantan for his first term from July 8, 2023, to July 7 this year, and has also served as MP for Pasir Mas and Bachok.

items.title: Sabah Fire Dept: Missing 11‑year‑old girl found drowned in Sungai Bengkoka after search launched for five victims
items.summary: Pitas Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) chief Noor Jali Maslah, in a statement today, said the victim was found by villagers at 7.36am, about one kilometre from the Fire and Rescue Control Centre (PKB). Noor Jali said the search and rescue (SAR) operation was launched after the station received an emergency call at 5.17pm yesterday regarding an incident involving five victims in the river. He said six personnel from BBP Pitas conducted the operation using a National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA) boat, employing the Surface Water Rescue method within a one-kilometre search radius from the PKB.

items.title: Fire Dept launches search after four teenage boys feared drowned at Tanjung Lompat Beach in Johor
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 2 — Four 16-year-old boys are feared to have drowned while swimming at Tanjung Lompat Beach, Tanjung Balau, Penawar, this morning. The Johor Fire and Rescue Department Operations Centre said it received an emergency call at 8.19am, after which six personnel from the Bandar Penawar Fire and Rescue Station were deployed to the scene. “Initial information from members of the public indicated that six victims had got into difficulties while swimming at the beach.

items.title: Samarahan moves out of hazardous category as Sarawak haze eases slightly
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 2 — Samarahan moved out of the Hazardous air quality category this morning after its Air Pollutant Index (API) reading fell from 302 at 8am to 292 at 10am. The latest reading placed Samarahan in the Very Unhealthy category, marking one of the more notable improvements recorded across Sarawak on Wednesday morning. Kanowit remained unchanged at 323, while Kuching’s API reading stayed at 318.

items.title: Six areas in Sabah record unhealthy API readings with KK Polytechnic highest at 185
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 2 — Six areas in Sabah recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 8 am today, with the Kota Kinabalu Polytechnic station recording the highest reading at 185. According to the Sabah State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) daily El Nino Monitoring infographic report, Kota Kinabalu recorded an API reading of 179, followed by Kimanis at 175, Keningau at 173, Sandakan at 152 and Tawau at 123. The report stated that API readings between 101 and 200 are categorised as unhealthy, with the public advised to reduce outdoor activities, while children, senior citizens and those with chronic illnesses are advised to avoid outdoor activities.

items.title: Alleged provocateur arrested for inciting crowd crush at National Day parade in Putrajaya
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — A 30-year-old cook has been arrested for allegedly inciting a crowd to breach security barriers to secure seats during the National Day 2026 celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya. The suspect was detained in Putrajaya yesterday afternoon after five police reports were lodged against him for instigating members of the public to push through the gates early on Aug 31, NST reported. Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus confirmed the arrest, adding that investigators will apply for a remand order against the suspect today.

items.title: MACC seeks to remand ex-minister over Tabung Haji Saudi Arabia hotel issue
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 2 — A former minister arrived at the Magistrate’s Court here today for remand proceedings in connection with investigations into the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) Report on Tabung Haji (TH). The man, in his 60s, arrived at 10.25 am wearing an orange Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) remand shirt. The TH RCI report was made public on July 29, documenting various weaknesses in TH’s management and operations between 2014 and 2020, as well as listing problematic investments requiring a forensic audit.

items.title: Malaysian Embassy in Doha issues advisory following US-Iran strikes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — The Malaysian Embassy in Doha has advised Malaysians in Qatar to stay abreast of developments and any notices issued by the Qatari authorities following the latest developments in the region. The embassy, in a notice posted on Facebook, also reminded individuals travelling from or transiting through Qatar to check the latest flight schedules to ensure a smooth journey. According to international media reports, the United States (US) launched its latest strikes on Iran on Tuesday, followed by retaliatory attacks by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) against US bases and assets in the region, further escalating tensions in West Asia.

items.title: Night closures on Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu Expressway in Penang from Sept 7 to 9
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 2 — The George Town-bound stretch of the Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu Expressway will undergo temporary nightly closures and traffic diversions from Sept 7 to 9 to facilitate ongoing highway construction works. The temporary disruption is to allow for the construction of an elevated U-turn facility, which is designed to complement the upcoming Air Itam Bypass and ease overall traffic congestion along the Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu Expressway. Motorists travelling towards George Town during these hours are advised to plan their journeys in advance, adhere strictly to on-site directional traffic signage, and drive with caution when approaching the construction zone to ensure public safety.

items.title: Malaysia hosts Asean health ministers’ meet again after 20 years
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — Malaysia will play host to the 17th Asean Health Ministers’ Meeting and Related Meetings (AHMM) scheduled to take place from Sept 7 to 11. The Ministry of Health (MOH), in a Facebook post, said the health meeting will carry the theme, ‘Healthy Asean: Together Towards Equitable, Future-Ready Health Systems.’ “Let us together support efforts towards a more equitable, resilient, and future-ready Asean health system,” the post read.

items.title: Sarawak haze persists: Serian, Kuching, Samarahan in ‘Hazardous’ zone
items.summary: Meanwhile, five areas in Sarawak recorded API readings of very unhealthy levels, namely Sibu (292), Sarikei (283), Mukah (241), Bintulu (226), and Sri Aman (214). Also recording unhealthy readings were Miri, Sarawak (181), Kota Kinabalu, Sabah (179), Kimanis, Sabah (175), Keningau, Sabah (173), Limbang, Sarawak (173), Johan Setia, Selangor (161), Sandakan, Sabah (152), Putrajaya (148), Nilai, Negeri Sembilan (137), Tawau, Sabah (123), and Seremban, Negeri Sembilan (116). Meanwhile, 44 stations recorded readings at moderate levels.
